content:
Hollywood is increasingly viewing YouTube as a major competitor, and according to a new report, free ad-supported streaming services may be the answer, with platforms such as Disney+ and Paramount+ considering launching them.

Streaming platforms such as Disney+, Paramount+ and Netflix are exploring the launch of free ad-supported tiers in different ways.

Recently, it was reported that Disney's Chief Product and Technology Officer Adam Smith discussed "providing free ad-supported content" at an internal streaming business meeting.

The move aims to remove the limitations of Disney+'s paywall in order to expand reach. Disney would then be able to more easily upsell paid subscription plans to users already using the app.

Paramount reportedly has a similar idea: "According to an internal briefing obtained by Business Insider, Paramount's flagship streaming platform plans to expand the range of films and programmes available to non-subscribers."

Netflix's comments on free services have mainly targeted markets outside the US. But depending on how the free ad-supported tiers of other streaming platforms perform, the situation could change at any time.

Each streaming platform has been driven to some extent by YouTube's growing user engagement and market share. Disney+ had previously planned to incorporate YouTube-like user-generated content and offer it for free. However, with the Sora project being scrapped and Disney's partnership with OpenAI falling through, the prospects for these plans have become uncertain.

What do you think about streaming platforms launching more free ad-supported tiers? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
